mainTopic: Reading the מגילה with or without ten, which observances are moved earlier or later, and the meaning of 'all the time of חגיגה'
overview: This amud opens by finishing an earlier point: even when the מגילה reading is moved earlier, the שמחה of פורים stays on its real date. רב rules that on the real date one may read the מגילה alone, but on a moved date ten are needed. רב אסי requires ten in both cases. The גמרא challenges רב from his statement 'ערב שבת זמנם', and then explains that this statement only rejects רבי's move to יום הכניסה. A new משנה defines a large city as one with ten בטלנין. It teaches that the מגילה is moved earlier, never later, while עצי כהנים, תשעה באב, חגיגה and הקהל are moved later, never earlier. The גמרא gives reasons: ״וְלֹא יַעֲבוֹר״ for the מגילה, not rushing tragedy for תשעה באב, and the obligation not yet having begun for חגיגה and הקהל. It then brings three readings of a ברייתא's phrase 'all the time of חגיגה', from רב אושעיא, רבא and רב אשי. The amud ends by starting a list of unusual practices of רבי, beginning with his planting on פורים.

steps.title: פורים joy stays on its real date
steps.stepSummary: The tail end of an earlier discussion: the שמחה of פורים is only on its proper date, even if the reading was moved.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rejoicing (of פורים) is only practiced on its proper date.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a point from the previous daf. Even when villages read the מגילה early, the celebration itself stays on the real day of פורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The early reading was a special allowance for the reading. The שמחה (feasting and joy) is not moved along with it; it stays on the real date of פורים.

keyTerms.meaning: Rejoicing, meaning the festive celebration of פורים
Is not practiced / does not apply
In its proper time (the real date)

phrases.english: The rejoicing (of Purim)
phrases.notes: This picks up a sentence that started on the previous daf.

phrases.english: is practiced only in its proper time.

steps.triggerLanguage: שִׂמְחָה, אֵינָהּ נוֹהֶגֶת אֶלָּא בִּזְמַנָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion carried over from the previous daf.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Moving the reading earlier does not move the שמחה; it stays on the real date.

steps.title: רב: alone on the real date, ten on a moved date
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that on its proper date the מגילה may be read privately, but on a moved date it requires ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: On its proper date, the מגילה may be read even by one person alone. When it is not on its proper date, it needs ten people.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב gives a rule about when you need a group of ten to read the מגילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the real date (the fourteenth), the מצוה applies to each person, so one can read alone. Reading early (for example on יום הכניסה) was an allowance made for a community. Because of that, a moved reading needs a group of ten.

keyTerms.meaning: Not in its proper time (a moved date)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not in its time' here does NOT mean a wrong or invalid date. It means one of the permitted alternate dates, like the villages reading early on יום הכניסה.

phrases.english: Rav said:
The Megillah in its proper time —
one may read it even alone;
not in its proper time — (only) with ten.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: מְגִילָּה בִּזְמַנָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the מנין requirement for reading the מגילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Proper date: an individual may read. Moved date: a מנין of ten is required.

steps.title: רב אסי: always ten
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי disagrees and requires ten whether or not it is the proper date.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said: Whether on its proper date or not on its proper date, it needs ten.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different opinion. רב אסי says the מגילה always needs a group of ten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי does not draw רב's line between the real date and a moved date. For him, reading the מגילה is always a public reading that needs ten, likely because publicizing the miracle is central to it.

phrases.english: Rav Asi said:
Both in its proper time and not in its proper time —
(it must be read) with ten.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַסִּי אָמַר: בֵּין בִּזְמַנָּהּ בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא בִּזְמַנָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues with רב's distinction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מנין of ten is always required for reading the מגילה.

steps.title: רב acts stringently for רב אסי's view
steps.stepSummary: In a real case, רב was concerned for רב אסי's opinion and read with ten even on the proper date.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an incident, and רב was concerned for this opinion of רב אסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story. When רב actually had to read on פורים itself, he gathered ten people, to satisfy רב אסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By his own rule, רב could have read alone on the real date. In practice he was stringent and took רב אסי's view into account. This shows his ruling was a basic rule, but he still preferred to be careful.

keyTerms.meaning: There was an incident (a real case)
He was concerned for (took into account)

phrases.english: There was an incident,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַשׁ לֵיהּ רַב לְהָא דְּרַב אַסִּי.
phrases.english: and Rav was concerned for this (view) of Rav Asi.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲוָה עוֹבָדָא, וְחַשׁ לֵיהּ רַב לְהָא דְּרַב אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how רב acted in practice given רב אסי's disagreement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In practice רב read with ten even on the proper date, out of concern for רב אסי.

steps.title: Did רב really say that? His other statement about פורים on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether רב required ten on a moved date. It quotes his statement that when פורים falls on שבת, ערב שבת is their time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רב really say this? But רב יהודה, son of רב שמואל בר שילת, said in the name of רב: When פורים falls on שבת, ערב שבת is their time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a challenge against רב. Here it only brings the quote. The next two steps explain why this quote is a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The formula 'ומי אמר רב הכי' signals that another statement of רב seems to contradict his rule. The quote calls Friday 'their time' (זמנם), even though Friday is a moved date. The גמרא will build on that word.

keyTerms.meaning: Did רב really say this? (opens a contradiction)

phrases.english: And did Rav say this?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Yehuda, son of Rav Shmuel bar Shilat, say
in the name of Rav:
Purim that falls on Shabbat —
Shabbat eve is their time.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַב הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's rule from step 2 using another of his statements.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that a moved-date reading needs ten.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: רב elsewhere calls the moved date (Friday) 'their time'. The next steps show this implies the moved date is treated like the real date.

steps.title: Isn't Shabbat itself the real date?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא wonders at רב's wording: why call Friday 'their time' when the real date is שבת?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is ערב שבת their time?! Isn't שבת their time!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רב's wording is strange. This sets up the next step, where the strange wording becomes the basis of the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real date of פורים in this case is שבת. Friday is only an early substitute. So when רב calls Friday 'זמנם', he must be teaching something more by that word.

phrases.english: Shabbat eve is their time?!
But Shabbat is their time!

steps.triggerLanguage: עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת זְמַנָּם?! וְהָא שַׁבָּת זְמַנָּם הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines the wording of the quote just brought.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does רב call Friday 'their time' when שבת is the real date?

steps.title: So the moved date is like the real date, even alone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests רב meant that a moved date counts like the proper date, so even an individual may read. This contradicts his rule requiring ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't this what he meant: Not in its time is like its time. Just as in its time it may be read even alone, so too not in its time it may be read even alone?
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge is now complete. If Friday has the full status of 'its time', then reading alone should be allowed on Friday, which goes against רב's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'זמנם' is read as a comparison: the moved date gets the same laws as the real date. One law of the real date (by רב himself) is that one may read alone. So the moved date should allow reading alone too, which contradicts step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it that... (pushes an inference)

phrases.english: Rather, isn't this what he meant:
Not in their time is like their time.
Just as in their time — even alone,
so too not in their time — even alone?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו הָכִי קָאָמַר: שֶׁלֹּא בִּזְמַנָּם כִּזְמַנָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the strange wording into a direct contradiction of רב's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule (step 2) that a moved-date reading needs ten.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Calling Friday 'their time' makes the moved date equal to the real date. The real date allows reading alone, so the moved date should too.

steps.title: No, that statement is not about a minyan
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the inference: רב's 'ערב שבת זמנם' was not said about reading with ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. (That statement was not said) regarding reading the מגילה with ten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב. The quote from step 5 has nothing to do with the מנין question, so it cannot contradict him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that 'זמנם' gives the moved date every law of the real date. The גמרא says the word was not about the מנין at all. The next step explains what it was really about.

phrases.english: No, (it was not said) regarding reading the Megillah with ten.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, לְעִנְיַן מִקְרָא מְגִילָּה בַּעֲשָׂרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers by rejecting the inference drawn in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading 'זמנם' as a statement about the מנין requirement.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenge wrongly assumed that 'their time' gives the moved date every law of the real date.

steps.title: רב was rejecting רבי's view
steps.stepSummary: רב's 'ערב שבת זמנם' only teaches that Friday, and not יום הכניסה, is the date for these towns. This rejects רבי's view that once displaced, they move to יום הכניסה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does 'ערב שבת is their time' mean? It excludes the view of רבי, who said: Since the towns were already pushed off their usual date, let them be pushed to the day of assembly. רב teaches us that ערב שבת is their time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the real meaning of רב's statement. He is answering a question about which day to read on, not how many people are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי argued that once these towns cannot read on their real date, they might as well move to יום הכניסה (Thursday) like the villages. רב disagrees: they move only one day, to Friday, the day right before. So 'זמנם' means 'the correct day for them', and רב's rule requiring ten on a moved date stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The day of assembly (Monday or Thursday, when villagers came to town)
This is what he teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: רב's rule stands: on the real date one may read alone, but on a moved date ten are needed. 'ערב שבת זמנם' only fixes Friday as the reading date when פורים falls on שבת, against רבי's move to יום הכניסה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that calling a date 'זמנם' can mean only 'the right day', without giving it every law of the real date. This is the difference between a date's category and how its laws are applied.

phrases.english: Rather, what is (meant by) 'Shabbat eve is their time'?
To exclude (the view) of Rebbi, who said:
Since the towns were pushed from their place (usual date) —
let them be pushed to the day of assembly;
this (Rav) teaches us
that Shabbat eve is their time.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת זְמַנָּם — לְאַפּוֹקֵי מִדְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer by giving the true purpose of רב's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the challenging source: it deals with which day to read, not with the מנין.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'זמנם' meant the moved date has every law of the real date, including reading alone.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'זמנם' only sets Friday as the reading day, rejecting רבי's move to יום הכניסה; רב's מנין rule is not contradicted.

steps.title: What counts as a large city
steps.stepSummary: The משנה defines an עיר גדולה as any place with ten בטלנין. With fewer, it is treated as a כפר.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: What is a 'large city'? Any place that has ten idlers. If it has fewer than that, it counts as a village.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It tells us what makes a place a 'large city' rather than a 'village' for reading the מגילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, villages could read early on the יום הכניסה, while cities read on the fourteenth. Now the משנה gives the test for which is which. The test is not how many people live there, but whether there are ten בטלנין.

keyTerms.meaning: A large city, which reads the מגילה on the fourteenth of אדר
Idlers: men free from work who are available for communal needs
A village, which may read early on the day of assembly

steps.confusionAlert: This 'large city' is NOT the same as a walled city (מוקף חומה), which reads on the fifteenth. Here the question is only whether a place counts as a city that reads on the fourteenth, or as a village that may read early.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ אִי זוֹ הִיא עִיר גְּדוֹלָה
phrases.english: MISHNA: What is a large city?
Any place that has ten idlers in it
Fewer than this, it is a village

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי זוֹ הִיא עִיר גְּדוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the previous discussion of רב's 'ערב שבת זמנם' closed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A place with ten בטלנין is an עיר גדולה. With fewer, it is a כפר even if it has many residents.

steps.title: מגילה is moved earlier, but some other dates are moved later
steps.stepSummary: For מגילה readings the rule is מקדימין ולא מאחרין. In contrast, עצי כהנים, תשעה באב, חגיגה and הקהל are pushed later, never earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was about these that they said: we move it earlier, not later. But the priests' wood-offering day, תשעה באב, the חגיגה offering, and הקהל are moved later, not earlier.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a direction rule. When the מגילה's date must move, it moves earlier. But a list of other special days moves later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מגילה must never be read after its proper time, so any shift goes backward. The four other observances are the opposite: when their day falls on שבת, they are delayed until after שבת. The משנה is contrasting two kinds of moved dates.

keyTerms.meaning: Days when priestly families donated wood for the מזבח and treated the day as a festival
The fast of the Ninth of אב
The gathering in the מקדש after שמיטה to hear the king read ספר דברים

phrases.english: About these they said
We move it earlier and do not move it later
But the time of the priests' wood offering
And the Ninth of Av, the festival offering, and the assembly
We move them later and do not move them earlier

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּאֵלּוּ אָמְרוּ מַקְדִּימִין וְלֹא מְאַחֲרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with the rule about which direction displaced dates move.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מגילה readings are moved earlier only. עצי כהנים, תשעה באב, חגיגה and הקהל are moved later only.

steps.title: An early reading day is not fully פורים
steps.stepSummary: Even when the reading is moved earlier, הספד and תענית are still allowed on that day. מתנות לאביונים, however, are given on that day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though they said we move it earlier and not later, eulogies and fasting are permitted on that day. And gifts to the poor are given then.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה clarifies how the early reading day is treated. It is not a real פורים, so mourning practices are not banned. But the poor still receive their gifts that day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moving the reading earlier moves only the reading itself, not the festive status of the day. So הספד and תענית stay permitted. מתנות לאביונים go with the reading, because the poor are waiting for them.

keyTerms.meaning: Gifts to the poor, a פורים obligation

phrases.english: Even though they said
We move it earlier and not later
They are permitted to eulogize and to fast
And gifts to the poor are given

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ מַקְדִּימִין וְלֹא מְאַחֲרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the practical status of the early reading day introduced in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An early reading day permits הספד and תענית, but מתנות לאביונים are given on it.

steps.title: רבי יהודה limits early reading
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says villages may read early only where villagers come to town on Mondays and Thursdays. Elsewhere, the מגילה is read only on its proper date.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: When does this apply? In a place where people come into town on Monday and Thursday. But in a place where they do not come in on Monday or Thursday, it is read only at its proper time.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds a condition to the early reading for villages. Early reading is allowed only where Monday and Thursday are market days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Villages were allowed to read early so they could hear the מגילה when they came to town for market and court days. If villagers do not come in on those days, the reason disappears. So they must read on the fourteenth like everyone else.

keyTerms.meaning: Monday and Thursday, the regular market and court days
The 'day of entering,' when villagers come to town
At its proper time (the fourteenth of אדר)

steps.whatToRemember: The early reading for villages depends on their coming to town on Mondays and Thursdays. According to רבי יהודה, without that practice, there is no early reading.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said: When does this apply?
In a place where they come into town on Monday and Thursday
But in a place where they do not come in
Neither on Monday nor on Thursday
They read it only at its proper time

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: אֵימָתַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limiting condition to the early-reading rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Early reading applies only where villagers come to town on Mondays and Thursdays. Otherwise, the מגילה is read only on the fourteenth.

steps.title: The ten idlers are men who sit in the בית הכנסת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא explaining that the ten בטלנין are men who are free to sit in the בית הכנסת.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It was taught: ten idlers who are in the synagogue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by explaining a word from the משנה. It uses a ברייתא to define who the 'ten idlers' are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בטלנין' does not mean lazy people. It means men without other work responsibilities who are always present in the בית הכנסת for communal needs. Having ten such men is what makes a place a city.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים not included in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: 'Idlers' here is not an insult. They are men who are free to always be in the בית הכנסת, so a מנין is always available.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught:
Ten idlers who are in the synagogue

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: עֲשָׂרָה בַּטְלָנִין שֶׁבְּבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא returns to the first line of the משנה (step 10) to define 'בטלנין'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ten בטלנין are ten men who are free to sit in the בית הכנסת and serve the community.

steps.title: Why is the מגילה read early but never late?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that the מגילה reading may be moved earlier but not later, and asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'With regard to these, they said we move it earlier and not later.' What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה and asks for its source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave the rule (Step 11) but no reason. The question is: why may we read early, for example on the יום הכניסה, but never after the proper date?

keyTerms.meaning: 'With regard to these they said', a quote of the משנה's wording

phrases.english: With regard to these, they said: we move it earlier and not later.
What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the rule from Step 11 to ask for its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural or logical source for the rule that the מגילה is read early but never late.

steps.title: The verse says 'and it shall not pass'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא in the name of שמואל brings the verse ״וְלֹא יַעֲבוֹר״ (אסתר ט:כז): the days of פורים must not pass without the reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said in the name of שמואל: the verse says, 'and it shall not pass.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a verse from מגילת אסתר. The time for the reading must not go by unfulfilled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״וְלֹא יַעֲבוֹר״ means the proper day may not pass without the reading. So reading late is forbidden. Reading early does not break this rule, because the day has not passed yet.
steps.whyThisMatters: This verse is the basis for the rule that the מגילה is never read after its proper time.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said in the name of Shmuel:
The verse says: 'And it shall not pass.'
phrases.notes: The set time shouldn't go by without reading the מגילה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא ״וְלֹא יַעֲבוֹר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse ״וְלֹא יַעֲבוֹר״ forbids letting the time pass, so the reading may be moved earlier but never later.

steps.title: Years are counted by months, not by days
steps.stepSummary: A second teaching of רבי אבא in the name of שמואל: a year is measured in months, not in a count of days, based on ״לְחׇדְשֵׁי הַשָּׁנָה״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אבא said in the name of שמואל: How do we know that we do not count days to make up years? Because it says, 'of the months of the year.' You count months to make up years, but you do not count days to make up years.
steps.whatsHappening: Since it just quoted רבי אבא in the name of שמואל, the גמרא adds another of his teachings, this one about the calendar. It is a side point, not part of the פורים discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Jewish year is 12 or 13 months, not a fixed number of days such as 365. The verse ties the year to months: ״לְחׇדְשֵׁי הַשָּׁנָה״.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not count days to make up years
'Of the months of the year' (שמות יב:ב)

steps.confusionAlert: This teaching is not connected to the topic of פורים. It appears here only because it is from the same teachers, רבי אבא in the name of שמואל.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Abba said in the name of Shmuel:
From where do we know that we do not count days to make up years?
As it says: 'Of the months of the year.'
Months you count to make up years,
but you do not count days to make up years.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side teaching added because it comes from the same teachers as Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Years are measured by months, not by a total count of days.

steps.title: Months are counted by days, not by hours
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן of קיסרי, in the name of רבי אבא: a month is measured in whole days, not in the exact hours of the moon's cycle, based on ״עַד חֹדֶשׁ יָמִים״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the rabbis of קיסרי said in the name of רבי אבא: How do we know that we do not calculate hours for months? Because it says, 'until a month of days.' You calculate days for months, but you do not calculate hours for months.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a matching calendar teaching. Just as years are made of months, months are made of whole days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The moon's cycle is about 29½ days. But a calendar month is a whole 29 or 30 days, not counted to the exact hour. The words 'month of days' tie the month to days.
steps.whatToRemember: Year = months, not days. Month = days, not hours.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּנַן דְּקֵיסָרִי מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמְרוּ:
phrases.english: And the rabbis of Caesarea said in the name of Rabbi Abba:
From where do we know that we do not calculate hours for months?
As it says: 'Until a month of days.'
Days you calculate for months,
but you do not calculate hours for months.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן דְּקֵיסָרִי מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel teaching to Step 17, moving one level down from years to months.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Months are measured in whole days, not by exact hours.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: observances that are only delayed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה: עצי כהנים, תשעה באב, חגיגה and הקהל are pushed later, never earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the time of the priests' wood offering, תשעה באב, the חגיגה, and הקהל are pushed later and not earlier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the side point and quotes the next part of the משנה. This sets up the explanations that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These observances follow the opposite rule from the מגילה. When their date falls on שבת, they move to after שבת, never before. The next steps explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: The days when certain families donated wood for the מזבח
The gathering of the nation to hear the Torah read by the king
We delay and do not move earlier

phrases.english: But the time of the priests' wood offering,
and the Ninth of Av, the festival offering, and the Hakhel assembly,
are delayed and not moved earlier.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל זְמַן עֲצֵי כֹהֲנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the calendar side point and returns to the משנה (Step 11).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These four observances are moved later, never earlier.

steps.title: תשעה באב: we do not rush tragedy
steps.stepSummary: תשעה באב is pushed later because we do not bring a day of calamity closer.
steps.simpleTranslation: תשעה באב: we do not bring calamity earlier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why תשעה באב is delayed rather than moved earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תשעה באב is a day of disaster. Moving it earlier would bring the sad day closer, so we push it off as long as we can.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not bring calamity earlier

phrases.english: The Ninth of Av:
we do not bring calamity earlier.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַקְדּוֹמֵי פּוּרְעָנוּת לָא מַקְדְּמִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the first item explained from Step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: תשעה באב is delayed because one does not hasten calamity.

steps.title: חגיגה and הקהל: their time has not yet come
steps.stepSummary: חגיגה and הקהל cannot be moved earlier because their obligation has not started yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: חגיגה and הקהל: because the time of their obligation has not yet arrived.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why חגיגה and הקהל are delayed. Before their date, there is no מצוה yet to fulfill.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike תשעה באב, the reason here is not about sadness. A מצוה cannot be done before its time begins. So the only option is to do it after the date.

keyTerms.meaning: The festival peace-offering brought on the רגלים

steps.whatToRemember: The מגילה goes earlier because of ״וְלֹא יַעֲבוֹר״. תשעה באב goes later so we do not rush tragedy. חגיגה and הקהל go later because a מצוה cannot be done before its time.

phrases.english: The festival offering and Hakhel:

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּאַכַּתִּי לָא מְטָא זְמַן חִיּוּבַיְיהוּ.
phrases.english: because the time of their obligation has not yet arrived.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּאַכַּתִּי לָא מְטָא זְמַן חִיּוּבַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the items of Step 19 with a different reason.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חגיגה and הקהל cannot be done early because their obligation has not yet begun.

steps.title: A ברייתא: The Festival Offering and Its Time Are Postponed
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that חגיגה and 'all the time of חגיגה' are pushed later, never earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: We push off the חגיגה, and also all the time of the חגיגה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds to our משנה's rule that חגיגה is pushed later. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא asks what the extra phrase means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה only said 'חגיגה is pushed later.' This ברייתא adds the words 'and all the time of חגיגה.' Those extra words need an explanation, and that is where the discussion goes next.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The time of the חגיגה.' The unclear phrase in this ברייתא.

phrases.english: It was taught: The Festival offering
and all the time of the Festival offering, we postpone.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: חֲגִיגָה וְכׇל זְמַן חֲגִיגָה מְאַחֲרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that expands the משנה's rule on postponing חגיגה, which was just discussed in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both חגיגה and 'the time of חגיגה' are pushed later.

steps.title: What Does 'The Time of the Festival Offering' Mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא understands why חגיגה is pushed past שבת but asks what 'the time of חגיגה' refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that the חגיגה is pushed off: if the festival falls on שבת, we push the offering until after שבת. But what is 'the time of the חגיגה'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the first half of the ברייתא is clear but the second half is not. It asks for an explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חגיגה cannot be brought on שבת, so it is moved to the days after. That part is simple. But 'the time of חגיגה' sounds like a stretch of time, not an offering, so it is unclear what is being postponed. This is a real request for information, not an attack.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is fine regarding…' The גמרא accepts one part before asking about another part.
It happens to fall (on a certain day).

phrases.english: Granted, the Festival offering is understood,
because if it falls on Shabbat
we postpone it until after Shabbat.
But 'the time of the Festival offering,' what is it?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא חֲגִיגָה, דְּאִי מִיקְּלַע בְּשַׁבְּתָא מְאַחֲרִינַן לַהּ לְבָתַר שַׁבְּתָא. אֶלָּא זְמַן חֲגִיגָה מַאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the unclear phrase in the ברייתא from step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is being postponed when the ברייתא says 'the time of חגיגה'?

steps.title: רב אושעיא: The עולת ראייה Is Postponed Even Past the יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא explains the ברייתא this way: חגיגה is pushed off because of שבת, and עולת ראייה is pushed off even because of יום טוב, even though יום טוב is the time of חגיגה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא said: This is what the ברייתא means. The חגיגה is pushed off when the festival is on שבת. The עולת ראייה is pushed off even when the festival is on יום טוב, even though that day is the time of the חגיגה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אושעיא answers the question by rereading the ברייתא. The phrase 'the time of חגיגה' is describing the day the עולת ראייה cannot be brought, not naming an offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two offerings and two different reasons for delay. The חגיגה, a שלמים offering, waits only because of שבת. The עולת ראייה, a burnt offering, waits even because of plain יום טוב. That is surprising, because יום טוב is the very day when the חגיגה may be brought. So 'the time of חגיגה' means: even on that day, the עולה is pushed off.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is what it means.' Used to reread a text in a new way.
The burnt offering brought when appearing at the בית המקדש on the festival.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'the time of חגיגה' as the name of a third offering. It describes a day: יום טוב is the time for the חגיגה, yet the עולת ראייה is still pushed off from it.

phrases.english: Rav Oshaya said: This is what it is saying:
The Festival offering is postponed on Shabbat,
and the burnt offering of appearance is postponed even on a Festival day,
which is the time of the Festival offering. We postpone it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא, הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'The time of חגיגה' refers to יום טוב. The עולת ראייה is pushed off even from that day, while the חגיגה is pushed off only because of שבת.

steps.title: Identifying the Author as בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that this ברייתא, as רב אושעיא explains it, follows the view of בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is the view of בית שמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names which תנא this ruling follows. This sets up the next step, where it quotes the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not everyone agrees that a burnt offering is forbidden on יום טוב. So the גמרא pins this ruling to one side of a known מחלוקת.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Whose is it?' This asks which תנא a teaching follows.

phrases.english: Whose view is this? It is Beit Shammai.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי — בֵּית שַׁמַּאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the author of the ruling as explained in step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא, as רב אושעיא explains it, follows בית שמאי.

steps.title: The Source: בית שמאי Forbid Burnt Offerings on a Festival
steps.stepSummary: The משנה in ביצה brings the מחלוקת. בית שמאי allow שלמים on יום טוב without סמיכה, and forbid עולות. בית הלל allow both, with סמיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: בית שמאי say we may bring שלמים on יום טוב, but we do not lean our hands on them. We may not bring עולות at all. בית הלל say we may bring שלמים and עולות, and we may lean our hands on them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה to prove that בית שמאי forbid a burnt offering on יום טוב. That is exactly why the עולת ראייה must wait until after the festival day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שלמים are mostly eaten, so slaughtering them counts as preparing food, which is allowed on יום טוב. עולות are burned completely and not eaten, so בית שמאי forbid them on יום טוב. That fits רב אושעיא: the חגיגה (a שלמים) may be brought on יום טוב, but the עולת ראייה is pushed off.

keyTerms.meaning: Peace offerings, most of which are eaten.
Burnt offerings, burned completely on the מזבח.
Leaning one's hands with force on the animal's head (סמיכה).

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אושעיא, the ברייתא follows בית שמאי. The חגיגה (a שלמים) waits only because of שבת. The עולת ראייה (an עולה) waits even past יום טוב, because בית שמאי forbid עולות on יום טוב.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that 'pushed later' can have different causes for different offerings. It also ties our ברייתא to the famous מחלוקת בית שמאי ובית הלל about sacrifices on יום טוב.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna: Beit Shammai say:
We may bring peace offerings on a Festival day,
but we do not lean our hands on them,
but not burnt offerings.
And Beit Hillel say:
We may bring peace offerings and burnt offerings
and we lean our hands on them.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: מְבִיאִין שְׁלָמִים בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source that proves the identification in step 25.
steps.raayaObject: That the ruling as explained by רב אושעיא follows בית שמאי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in ביצה 19a: בית שמאי forbid עולות on יום טוב, while בית הלל permit them.

steps.title: רבא: Push it off within the festival, but no later
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains 'all the time of חגיגה' as the time limit. You may push off the חגיגה throughout the festival days, but not past them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The חגיגה may be pushed off for the whole time of חגיגה, but not longer.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer to the question from Step 23 about what 'the time of חגיגה' means. He reads it as a deadline, not as a statement about יום טוב pushing anything off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב אושעיא, the phrase meant that עולת ראייה is pushed off even by יום טוב. That reading follows only בית שמאי. רבא reads the phrase as an outer limit: delay is allowed only within the days of the festival. With this reading, the ברייתא no longer has to follow בית שמאי.
steps.confusionAlert: 'כל זמן חגיגה' here does not mean something new is pushed off. It is the boundary for how long you may wait.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The festival offering may be postponed for the entire time of the festival offering,
longer than that, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: חֲגִיגָה, כׇּל זְמַן חֲגִיגָה — מְאַחֲרִין, טְפֵי — לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new reading of the ברייתא instead of רב אושעיא's, so the ברייתא need not follow בית שמאי.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does 'all the time of חגיגה' in the ברייתא mean?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is the time limit: you may postpone throughout the festival, but not beyond it.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה: The make-up period ends with the festival
steps.stepSummary: A משנה in חגיגה teaches that someone who missed the חגיגה on the first day may bring it all through the רגל. Once the רגל is over, he no longer owes it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: One who did not bring the חגיגה on the first day of the festival may keep bringing it the whole festival, including the last day. Once the festival has passed and he did not bring it, he is not responsible to make it up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to support רבא's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה shows that the חגיגה can be brought on any day of the festival. That is 'all the time of חגיגה.' It also shows that once the festival ends, the obligation is gone. That matches רבא's 'longer, no.'

keyTerms.meaning: may keep on bringing the חגיגה

phrases.english: As we learned: one who did not bring the festival offering
on the first festival day of the festival,

phrases.aramaic: חוֹגֵג וְהוֹלֵךְ אֶת כָּל הָרֶגֶל כּוּלּוֹ,
phrases.english: may continue to bring it throughout the entire festival,
and on the last festival day of the festival.
If the festival passed and he did not bring it,
he is not obligated to make it up.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: מִי שֶׁלֹּא חָג בְּיוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל חַג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's reading with a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that the חגיגה may be postponed during the festival but not after it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in חגיגה: one may bring it all the festival, and once the festival passes there is no obligation.

steps.title: רב אשי: Even one-day שבועות has make-up days
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that 'all the time of חגיגה' teaches that even עצרת (שבועות), which is only one day, allows the חגיגה to be postponed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The חגיגה may be postponed for the whole time of חגיגה. Even on עצרת, which is one day, we postpone it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a third reading of the extra words in the ברייתא. In his reading they teach something about שבועות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think that a one-day holiday like שבועות has no make-up period, so a חגיגה that cannot be brought that day is simply lost. רב אשי says the ברייתא's words 'all the time of חגיגה' teach that שבועות also has a make-up period, so its חגיגה is pushed later too. This reading also does not depend on בית שמאי.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
The festival offering and all the time of the festival offering, we postpone,
and even Shavuot, which is one day, we postpone,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: חֲגִיגָה וְכׇל זְמַן חֲגִיגָה — מְאַחֲרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further alternative to both רב אושעיא and רבא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does 'all the time of חגיגה' in the ברייתא mean?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It teaches that even one-day שבועות allows the חגיגה to be postponed.

steps.title: Proof: When שבועות is on שבת, slaughter is after שבת
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says that all agree: when שבועות falls on שבת, the day of slaughtering is after שבת. This shows that שבועות has a make-up day.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: They agree that if עצרת falls on שבת, the day of slaughter is after שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to prove רב אשי's point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קרבנות of the רגל cannot be brought on שבת, so they are brought on Sunday. Sunday is already after שבועות itself. This proves that the חגיגה of a one-day holiday can still be brought on a later day.

keyTerms.meaning: the day of slaughtering the festival offerings

steps.whatToRemember: There are three readings of 'all the time of חגיגה.' רב אושעיא: even יום טוב pushes off עולת ראייה (following בית שמאי). רבא: you may postpone only until the festival ends. רב אשי: even one-day שבועות has make-up days.

phrases.english: As we learned: they agree
that if Shavuot falls on Shabbat,
the day of slaughter is after Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: מוֹדִים שֶׁאִם חָל עֲצֶרֶת לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב אשי's reading with a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's claim that the חגיגה of one-day שבועות can be postponed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in חגיגה: when שבועות falls on שבת, the day of slaughter is after שבת.

steps.title: רבי planted a sapling on פורים
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר quotes רבי חנינא that רבי (יהודה הנשיא) planted a sapling on פורים. This opens a new set of reports about רבי's unusual practices.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי חנינא: רבי planted a sapling on פורים,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It begins a list of unusual things that רבי did. This is the first item, and the list continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Planting is a מלאכה. The fact that רבי planted on פורים raises the question of whether work is allowed on פורים. The גמרא will discuss this question next.

keyTerms.meaning: The festival of פורים, the fourteenth of אדר

steps.confusionAlert: 'רבי' alone means רבי יהודה הנשיא, the compiler of the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said that Rabbi Chanina said:
Rabbi planted a sapling on Purim,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: רַבִּי נָטַע נְטִיעָה בְּפוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, unrelated to the חגיגה discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי planted a sapling on פורים, implying that this kind of work did not concern him on that day.
